member.name: F:Cs2Gs.Pipeline.NullAssertionPolishPass.DefaultMaxRounds
member.summary:
Issue #3723: the round cap RunToFixedPoint stops at.
The loop cannot actually run forever — only ever DELETES !! tokens and a round that strips none breaks out, so the number of rounds is bounded by the number of assertions in the tree. The cap is a cost guard, not a termination guard, and hitting it is reported rather than silent.
Issue #3782: it used to be the binding constraint on any deep graph. One round can only strip what the compile it followed reported, and a warnings-as-errors compile reports nothing past the first project it fails on — so tools/cs2gs/Cs2Gs.Tests, which pulls twelve projects into its build, needed roughly one round per project (~40) and exhausted the cap with 14752 GS0536 still standing. The loop now SURVEYS instead: every round after the first demotes GS0536 to a warning (), so a single build walks the whole graph and reports every redundant assertion in it at once. Convergence is then a function of assertion NESTING (a!!.b!!), not of graph depth, and the cap stops being reachable.

member.name: F:Cs2Gs.Pipeline.SdkCompileRunner.MirroredTestRunSecondsPerDeclaredTest
member.summary:
Issue #3501: seconds of budget granted per [Fact] method declared by the app's C# original.
Calibrated against measurement, not taste. Two DIFFERENT measurements feed this constant, and every figure below is labelled with the one it came from — they were conflated once already, and a calibration record that mixes them is worse than no record:
CI — gate run 34232380469 (cs2gs-selfmig-nightly on main, Release, GitHub-hosted runner). The
MIGRATED test/Compiler.Tests, 4,103 declared [Fact] methods, completed and reported Failed: 79, Passed: 5415, Skipped: 0, Total: 5494. Its whole validation cost 4,864 s (~81 min), of which the test run was the dominant share at 3,658 s (~61 min): ~0.9 s per declared [Fact] for the run alone, ~1.2 s once the rest of validation is charged to the same count.
LOCAL — the C# ORIGINALS timed on a developer machine in Debug, which agree on the shape:
Cs2Gs.Tests 2,891 cases in 21 m 57 s (re-measured 2026-09-08) and Compiler.Tests 5,234 cases in 41 min (2026-09-06), ≈ 0.45 s per executed case. These case counts are local Debug numbers for the ORIGINALS and are NOT the CI run's totals above; the migrated build runs slower, and a declared count is lower than an executed count because a [Theory] expands. The rate is derived from the CI line alone — 4,103 declared facts over that run's ~81 minutes — so the executed-case counts are context, not inputs, and correcting one does not move the constant. 1.5 s/test is that observed rate with a ~50% margin for runner variance, which is enough to distinguish "large" from "stuck" without waiting out a real hang.

member.name: F:Cs2Gs.Pipeline.SdkCompileRunner.MirroredTestRunTimeout
member.summary:
Issue #3931: the FLOOR of the budget for a mirrored dotnet test run (see ). Named (rather than inline) so the parity stage can report the exact budget a killed run exceeded instead of describing a nameless timeout.
Issue #3501: this stayed the budget for EVERY app's test run until the corpus grew suites of a few thousand cases, at which point a single global constant stopped being a hang detector and became a size limit: the app was killed for being big, not for being stuck. It survives as the floor because a small suite that has not finished in ten minutes really is stuck, and a hang there must still fail promptly.

member.name: F:Cs2Gs.Pipeline.SdkCompileRunner.MirroredTestRunTimeoutCeiling
member.summary:
Issue #3501: the hard ceiling on a mirrored test budget, whatever the suite's size says it wants.
It started as the 90 minutes issue #4045 granted Compiler.Tests by hand. Issue #4633 raised it to 120: nightly 36906270739 measured the migrated Compiler.Tests run at 4,941 s, 91% of 90 minutes, so ordinary runner variance was enough to turn a healthy suite into a LIBRARY-TESTS-TIMED-OUT with no parity verdict at all. 120 minutes plus that app's ~25 minutes of compile and ILVerify still fits the 240-minute validation job with room for its shard-mates. The ceiling matters because a validation shard runs all of its apps under a single cs2gs validate process that writes shard-run.json only at the end (see build/run-cs2gs-selfmig-validate.sh), so a shard that overruns the job's 240-minute limit loses EVERY app's verdict — the same "no measurement at all" failure this sizing exists to remove, just one level up. An unbounded per-app budget would trade one app's missing parity count for a whole shard's.

A count of declared tests, by contrast, is a property of the source: it moves only when someone writes or deletes a test.

The gate above is deliberately narrow — it stops only when MSBuild could not open the project at all — because some corpus fixtures carry a deliberate C# error to exercise a later stage (CompileGap-Library's Residual.Probe). The cost of that narrowness was that a project whose C# genuinely does NOT bind was translated anyway, silently and with no signal: CSharpProjectLoader.SignificantDiagnostics already collected the errors into , but nothing past the workspace gate ever looked at them.

Reporting is non-fatal so the deliberate-error fixtures keep exercising the stages after this one, and no triage artifact is produced so run fingerprints and the gap ledger are unchanged.

member.name: T:Cs2Gs.Pipeline.CanonicalRootPath
member.summary:
Resolves a migration root to its real, symlink-free absolute path (issue #3732).
) normalizes ./.. and makes a path absolute, but it does NOT follow symbolic links, so a root given as /tmp/… on macOS (where /tmp and $TMPDIR are both links) stays spelled through the link. Every path the pipeline derives from that root — the mirrored .gsproj files and the ProjectReference paths between them — then inherits that spelling, while MSBuild/NuGet reach the same files through their real path. NuGet keys restore graph nodes by absolute path, so the two spellings become two nodes: the referencing project's project.assets.json comes back with an EMPTY projectReferences/libraries set and none of the referenced project's packages flow to it.
C# survives that silently — csc only needs the assemblies a compilation actually names — but gsc reads referenced assemblies through a , which must resolve the whole AssemblyRef closure of every reference. A package that a referenced project uses only inside a method body is therefore mandatory for gsc and absent from csc's needs, and the split root surfaces as GS9997 Could not find assembly '<package>' on exactly the projects whose only route to that package is a ProjectReference.
The gate scripts already canonicalize their work root with pwd -P (build/run-cs2gs-selfmig-migrate.sh); this does the same for a hand-run cs2gs migrate --out /tmp/… / cs2gs validate --migrated /tmp/…, which is the documented reproduction recipe.

member.name: T:Cs2Gs.Pipeline.RepositoryVerbatimSources

member.remarks:
A .cs file is translated when a translated project compiles it, or, failing that, as an orphan. That is wrong for a .cs file a project references as DATA or as foreign input rather than as source it compiles: a None/Content/EmbeddedResource item (translation-test fixtures a test reads as text) or a Compile item of an already-G# project (ForeignCompile.gsproj lists ThisAssembly.cs for the SDK to translate at build time). The rule: a .cs file matched by any item of a repository project file other than a Compile item of a translated (.csproj, shared .props/.targets) project is copied verbatim. A file that is both (compiled by a translated project AND referenced as data) is translated and ALSO copied. Item operations are applied in document order per item type, as MSBuild does. Includes that cannot be resolved statically (unknown MSBuild properties) and explicitly name .cs files are reported as warnings rather than guessed at.

member.name: T:Cs2Gs.Pipeline.TestNameParity
member.summary:
Issue #4633: compares the C# original's discovered test-case names () with the test cases the migrated run actually executed (its TRX), name for name.
Names are compared as MULTISETS: two theory rows whose arguments render identically are two cases on both sides, so one of them vanishing is still a missing case.
One asymmetry is inherent to comparing discovery with execution. xUnit pre-enumerates a [Theory] into one case per row only when every row's data is serializable; otherwise discovery reports ONE case, the bare method name, and execution reports a result per row (M(x: ...)). A bare C# name with no exact migrated match is therefore satisfied by one or more migrated rows of that method. Row COUNTS of such theories cannot be checked against discovery (the C# side never enumerated them); every other case, every pre-enumerated row included, is checked exactly.

member.name: T:Cs2Gs.Pipeline.TestNameParityBaseline
member.summary:
Issue #4633: the register of KNOWN per-test-name differences between a C# test project and its migrated run, each justified on its own line, so the strict per-name check can land green while the differences it found are tracked rather than hidden.
Four kinds of entry exist, and each excuses as little as possible:
missing: one exact C# display name the migrated run may lack, once (or count times, for a name
that legitimately occurs more than once).
extra: one exact migrated display name the C# oracle may lack, once (or count times).
rows: one theory METHOD (Ns.Class.Method, no argument list) whose rows render differently on
the two sides. It excuses that method's missing and extra rows ONLY when they pair up one for one by argument structure (the same multiset of argument-name lists, e.g. (x: …, y: …)), so it covers a value rendering differently between C# and G# and never a lost row hidden behind an unrelated added one.
renamed-argument: one theory METHOD whose parameter argument is named renamedTo in the
migrated build. It pairs a missing row with an extra row only when renaming that one argument label turns the first into exactly the second, so every value and every other label must still match.
Every entry needs a substantive reason and an issue. Entries that stop matching are reported as stale (advisory, like ), so the register shrinks as fixes land. It is a separate file from the failure allow-list because it answers a different question ("which cases exist" rather than "which cases may fail").

member.name: T:Cs2Gs.Pipeline.TestParityAllowList
member.summary: Issue #3885: the test-parity failure allow-list — the small, explicit set of migrated tests that are KNOWN to fail for a reason that is policy rather than defect, so a mirrored test run whose failures are a subset of it still reports green. The motivating class is a test that asserts on its OWN repository's source layout: test/Sdk.Tests reads Gsharp.NET.Sdk.csproj and matches Contains("SemaphoreSlim updateGate"). The migrated mirror correctly holds .gsproj and G# syntax, so those assertions cannot hold there — and relaxing them would weaken a real guard in the UNMIGRATED repository. Neither "fix the test" nor "fix the translator" applies; the premise "I am running in the C# repo" is deliberately untrue after migration. An allow-list is a hole in the gate by construction, so every rule here exists to keep the hole small, visible and self-maintaining: Individual tests only. An entry names one test, and rejects anything that could name more than one: no wildcards, and a name that is at least Class.Method. Matching is suffix-anchored at the METHOD (see ), so a namespace or class prefix can never match a test — allow-listing a whole app or a whole class is not expressible, not merely discouraged. Justification is mandatory. An entry without a substantive reason is a load error, not a silently-honoured entry. An unexplained entry is how a list rots. Report, never hide. carries the allowed failures out of the stage so the run record and the gate summary name them even on a PASS. Stale entries are detectable. An entry whose test did NOT fail in a completed run is reported as stale, mirroring how greenApps reports newly-green apps to bank. Subset, not intersection. partitions the failing set; the caller may only pass when is empty. "Some failures were allowed" is never enough.

The per-app hand-off between a translate-only migrate run and a later validate run over the same migrated tree (issue #3668).
Sharding the self-migration gate splits it into ONE whole-repository translate pass and N independent per-app validation shards. Translation must stay whole-repository — linked sources (e.g. test/Shared/*.cs) are compiled into several projects and cross-checks that they translate identically everywhere; splitting the translate pass would silently disable that guard. Stages 2–4 (compile, ilverify, test-parity), by contrast, only read the migrated tree, so they shard cleanly.
The only translate-derived state stages 2–4 consume in repository layout is captured here: the emitted .gs file set (compile-error attribution and the !! polish pass), the external reference paths (ilverify's -r set), and the project classification flags. The G# source text itself is NOT stored — it is read back from the migrated tree, which is exactly what a whole run would have on disk at that point.

member.name: T:GSharp.Tests.IlVerifyFilterInFinallyRule
member.summary:
Recognizes one known dotnet-ilverify 10.0.8 false positive (#4489, upstream https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/134711): a StackUnderflow reported at the first instruction of an exception FILTER block whose start lies physically inside a finally or fault handler.
Root cause: ILVerify's StartImportingBasicBlock checks a block's HandlerIndex before its FilterIndex, so a filter start that sits inside a finally/fault handler inherits that handler's empty entry stack instead of the exception object the CLR pushes. (Inside a catch handler it inherits the catch's exception type, which happens to verify.) Roslyn's IL for the same C# fails identically, and the code runs correctly.
The rule is deliberately narrow. It never ignores StackUnderflow as a category: the reported method must resolve in the assembly's metadata, the reported method identity (type, name, parameter count) must be unique in the assembly, the reported offset must equal one of its filter regions' FilterOffset, the instruction there must pop exactly one value, and the innermost handler region enclosing that offset must be Finally or Fault. Anything else, including a line this class cannot parse or resolve, stays an error.
Shared (linked source) between the Compiler.Tests IlVerifier and the cs2gs self-migration IlVerifyRunner.
